strings: Used to monitor the station's atmospherics sensors.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
A short engineering holographic barrier used for designating hazardous zones, slightly blocks radiation. Can only be passed by walking.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.

An ultra-futuristic, sleek, advanced, next-gen normal digital clock that tells the time. Powered by bluespace. Despite supposedly being better in every way to classic clocks, it just doesn't feel the same. They just don't make them the way they used to...
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
Mirror mirror on the wall, who's the most robust of them all?
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
Used to keep bodies in until someone fetches them. Includes a high-tech alert system.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A thin layer of dust coating the floor.
It's coarse and rough and gets everywhere.
Atmospherics Project Room Lockdown Blast Door
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
Now you see me, now you don't...
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
A set of Nanotrasen regulations for keeping law, order, and procedure followed within their space stations.
It's a normal black ink pen.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
It's a common fountain pen, with a faux wood body. Rumored to work in zero gravity situations.
Damn, they better have the /tg/ channel on these things.
A station intercom. It looks like it has been modified to not broadcast.

An industrial unit made to hold, charge, and decontaminate equipment. It comes with a built-in UV cauterization mechanism. A small warning label advises that organic matter should not be placed into the unit.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
A wrench with common uses. Can be found in your hand.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
Get a load, or give, of these all natural Xenos!
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A manifold composed of regular pipes.
A canister for the storage of gas.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
A portable variant of the station scrubbers, capable of filtering gas from the air around it or inserted tank. May also be wrenched into a port.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
A Prism-brand path illumination device. It is anchored in place and glowing steadily.
A piece of headgear used in dangerous working conditions to protect the head. Comes with a built-in flashlight AND welding shield! The bulb seems a little smaller though.
A small bottle of Choral Hydrate. Mickey's Favorite!
A small bottle of toxins. Do not drink, it is poisonous.
A syringe that can hold up to 15 units.
A small bottle. Contains a small amount of fluorosulfuric acid.
A dropper. Holds up to 5 units.
Used to remotely activate devices. Allows for syncing when using a secure signaler on another.
Contains condensed capsaicin for use in law \"enforcement.\"
It's a storage unit for rad-protective suits.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
The intergalactic symbol of medical institutions. You'll probably get help here.
Extremely sturdy exterior hull plating that separates you from the uncaring vacuum of space.
A mug to display your corporate pride.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A sign with the Nanotrasen logo on it. Glory to Nanotrasen!
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
An artistic poster commemorating 600 years of continual business for Cybersun Industries.
In Greek myth, Prometheus stole fire from the Gods and gave it to 		humankind. The jewelry he kept for himself.
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
A bamboo mat with a decorative trim.
Interdyne Pharmaceutics: For the Health of Humankind
An advertisement for Interdyne Pharmaceutics' GeneClean clinics. 'Become the master of your own body!'
This informational poster uses Safety Moth™ to tell the viewer to hide in lockers when the Supermatter Crystal has delaminated, to prevent hallucinations. Evacuating might be a better strategy.
A metallic frame that can hold tanks and extinguishers.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
Known for their milk, just don't tip them over.
A sign that warns of high-power testing equipment in the area.
Somehow, you can always find one under the wrestling ring.
A trash bin, place your trash here for the janitor to collect.
A reinforced version of the glass table.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
The HS-452. Installed in the 2550s by the Nanotrasen Hygiene Division, now with 2560 lead compliance! Passively replenishes itself with water when not in use.
Ew, I think I see a hairball.
No matter how much you squirm, it'll still be uncomfortable.
This cone is trying to warn you of something!
Perfectly designed to be comfortable to sit on, and hellish to sleep on.
All engineering related spawners go here
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
Old is never too old to not be in fashion.
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
For the bulkier art pieces, hand-picked by the curator.
This thing is all in Japanese.
A tank full of industrial welding fuel. Do not consume.
A standard edition welder provided by Nanotrasen.
A head-mounted face cover designed to protect the wearer completely from space-arc eye.
Protects the eyes from bright flashes; approved by the mad scientist association.

An ancient marble statue. The subject is depicted with a floor-length braid and is wielding a toolbox. By Jove, it's easily the most gorgeous depiction of a woman you've ever seen. The artist must truly be a master of his craft. Shame about the broken arm, though.
Do jump on it, it can take it.
A covered turret that shoots at its enemies.
A self cleaning vending machine capable of dispensing clothing for janitors.
A figurine depicting a Janitor with their galoshes.
Heats or cools gas in connected pipes.
A warning sign which reads 'RADSTORM SHELTER'.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with generic programs.
A great place for storing knowledge.
Ain't nobody gonna cheat the hangman in my town.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.

\"I'll sweeten thy sad grave: thou shalt not lack the flower that's like thy face, pale primrose, nor the azured hare-bell, like thy veins; no, nor the leaf of eglantine, whom not to slander, out-sweeten'd not thy breath.\"

Only one thing here is fertile, and it's not the eggs.
